data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek 'gaspan', meaning 'treasurer, holder of wealth', or the Latin 'gaspar', meaning 'treasurer'. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Gaspare usually hope their child will grow to embody treasurer, holder of wealth and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Gaspar
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Gaspar ex Aramaico videtur, quod significat strenuus et fortis homo. In historia Ecclesiae Christianae, Gaspar est nomen importantissimum, cum sanctus Gasparus, Episcopus Ancyranus, fuit primus qui Evangelium in Armenia promulgavit. Gaspar est nomen gentilitium ex Aramaico, quod significat vir fortis, vir strenuus, vir fortissimus. In historia Ecclesiae Christianae, Gaspar est memoriale sancti Gaspari Episcopi Ancyrani.

This story has been popularized through art, music, and literature, and the name Gaspare serves as a reminder of the profound impact of the Magi in Christian history and culture.
